rationales.1: Price, stock state and sowing window sit on a fixed line per entry so scanning is predictable, but the flat ungrouped list of eight makes season-first browsing depend entirely on the month select.
rationales.2: Price sits directly under the description, stock uses plain in-stock and out-of-stock language, and the product page puts quantity and Add to basket immediately under the price with nothing clever anywhere.
rationales.3: Out of stock is set apart in red, the unpriced packet reads Price pending — ask us with no invented figure, the germination estimate is labelled, and UK-only shipping is stated in the header of both surfaces.
rationales.4: The largest and airiest type of the set, single column at both widths, with no information carried by hover.
rationales.5: The most disciplined of the three: one rule language, one type scale and one palette carried identically across catalog and product page.
rationales.6: The year table, difficulty and germination line, potting-shed notes and companion packets are all present and ordered so a first-timer can decide without leaving the page.
rationales.7: A hand-kept numbered list you are asked to read slowly is a believable two-person conceit, though it stays closer to restraint than to a signature the whole page argues.
rationales.8: Novelty is limited to the numbered-list conceit and the letterpress voice; the money path is untouched.
rationales.9: Two of us keep this list and From our potting shed read as the shop rather than as a brand, warm and specific without hurry.
rationales.10: A returning shopper gets stock flags and a month select but no in-season or newly-stocked grouping, so re-orientation means a full scan of the list.
